hotspots.whyItMatters: Class A vs. Class B (survivability/supervision) pathway questions are classic fire-alarm-system material.
hotspots.cite: NFPA 72 — Circuits and Pathways chapter (confirm chapter number in your 2019 edition)
hotspots.trap: Assuming Class A is just a 'redundant loop' without recognizing it must survive a single open or ground fault and keep reporting every device.

hotspots.whyItMatters: Spacing and placement rules drive layout questions for detection coverage.
hotspots.cite: NFPA 72 — Initiating Devices chapter (confirm chapter number in your edition)
hotspots.trap: Applying open-area spacing rules to a room with obstructions (beams, high ceilings) without the required spacing adjustment.

hotspots.whyItMatters: Candela ratings and audible dBA-above-ambient rules are the notification-side counterpart to detector spacing.
hotspots.cite: NFPA 72 — Notification Appliances chapter (confirm chapter number in your edition)
hotspots.trap: Sizing a strobe by room area alone and skipping the mounting-height requirement that also governs compliance.

hotspots.whyItMatters: Exam questions often ask 'how often' for a given device or system test.
hotspots.cite: NFPA 72 — Inspection, Testing, and Maintenance chapter (confirm chapter number in your edition)
hotspots.trap: Using one blanket test interval for every device type instead of checking the device-specific frequency table.
